transcript:
Meeting: Econ & Cache Playbook Demo — Lighthouse Logistics
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Sarah (Lighthouse Head of ML), Tom (Platform Eng), Olivia (CTO)
Recording: https://redwood.fireflies/rec/ff-20260722-LL-001 (internal link)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on reducing per-token spend for low-latency routing use cases. Emphasized prefix/KV cache + batching tradeoffs and a sample cost model with dedicated pool options. Security/SSO/KMS questions answered at a high level; Redwood to share full pack.

Topics covered: cost model, batching windows, prefix cache TTLs, KV hit rate assumptions, dedicated vs hosted sizing, SLOs and fallback policies, pilot plan

-- Transcript --
00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for taking the time today, we've got about 50 minutes, we'll run through a targeted Optimize playbook focused on batching and cache, cost impacts, and then leave time for questions. Sound good?
00:09 Sarah (Lighthouse): Yep sounds great, we mostly want to validate cost numbers and make sure latency doesn't blow up during peak pickups, so priority is p50 under 200ms for short messages.
00:22 Diego (Redwood SE): Awesome. Quick context check — current infra? are you on GCP or AWS for inference?
00:27 Tom (Lighthouse): We're on AWS, mix of ECS and some EKS. Right now we send sync requests to OpenAI for responses, but it's pricey and the variability is killing budgets.
00:36 Maya: Got it. So we'll show how Optimize suggests batching and prefix/KV cache configs tuned for your sessionized workflows. We'll model both hosted and dedicated pricing.
00:47 Olivia (Lighthouse): Curious how you handle sticky sessions and cold starts, that's where our costs spike.
00:52 Diego: Great question. The playbook uses session affinity + prefix caching for repeated conversation context, and KV cache for large user state. We simulate hit rates to show dollar impact.
01:05 Sarah: When you say prefix cache, do you mean full prefix reuse or partial? like we have dynamic user notes appended each turn.
01:13 Diego: It's usually partial. Prefix cache handles the shared instructions and common prompt scaffolding, so you get high reuse across users for system prompts. KV cache stores per-session KV that we can attach to the runtime for quick KV-cache hits on the attention layer.
01:29 Tom: Sorry, quick dumb Q — is KV cache the same as session cache? And does it require sticky routing to a specific GPU?
01:36 Diego: Not exactly the same. KV cache is the model's key/value cache kept in memory to avoid recomputing. For persistent sessions you get better economics if you route to the same worker (session affinity), but Redwood Optimize can suggest eviction and fallback policies so you don't over-provision.
01:49 Maya: I'll show the cost table — rough numbers off the bat: with no caching and 1.5k tokens average per conversation, hosted calls to a baseline model are around $0.01 per request, batching and good KV hits can drop that to ~ $0.0025 per request in our sim. These are illustrative, Diego will run your numbers later.
02:11 Sarah: Those are promising. Does that assume quantization or a smaller model?
02:16 Diego: The baseline sim uses a 16-bit fp model. If you pick a quantized variant we can shave another ~15-30% CPU/GPU cost but you'll want to validate quality. Optimize recommends that as a second stage.
02:30 Tom: How about latency — when you batch to save cost doesn't p50 jump up?
02:34 Diego: There's a trade. We recommend dynamic batching with latency SLOs. For your p50 200ms target we model micro-batches and greedy flush thresholds. Example: at 8 concurrent connections a 16ms batching window buys you 2x token throughput but adds ~20-30ms tail in worst-case. If that's unacceptable we recommend smaller windows + prefix caching.
03:02 Olivia: If the 200ms is non-negotiable, what cost do we expect?
03:07 Maya: For dedicated pool with sessionization and ~60% prefix hit rate we project about $X per 1M tokens — in the spreadsheet we'll give concrete dollars; quick back-of-envelope for you it's roughly 40-60% lower than your current OpenAI spend in many of our sims.
03:22 Sarah: Can you explain the prefix hit rate assumptions? 60% seems high for our use case.
03:27 Diego: Sure. Prefix hit rate depends on how standardized your system prompts and how many tokens are user-specific. If earlier turns have static routing rules, and only last 50-100 tokens are dynamic user content, you can often hit 50-70% on the prefix. If you have long custom notes per user, hit rate drops. We ran an analysis on similar logistics chatbots and 45-55% was typical.
03:49 Tom: What about TTL for KV? If TTL is long we consume memory, how do we balance?
03:55 Diego: Right — Optimize suggests TTL + LRU eviction and a bloom-filtered prefetch heuristic. You can also do session weight based eviction: heavy users keep hot slots, light users get prefetch on demand.
04:08 Maya: I'll flip to the cost model slide — (brief pause) Note: these sims are traffic-shaped from your sample heatmap, we used peak QPS at 120 reqs/min and average tokens 300. With those numbers, enabling prefix cache with 50% hit and modest batching reduced cost per million tokens from about $2400 to $930 in the hosted sim.
04:36 Sarah: Again those numbers are huge — what's the sensitivity? If hit rate falls to 30%?
04:40 Diego: At 30% hit and same batching the sim shows cost around $1,560 per million tokens. The curve is fairly linear on the hit rate; batching helps more at higher concurrency.
04:51 Tom: On the dedicated side, how do you size the GPU pool? do you have templates?
04:56 Diego: Yes — Redwood has sizing templates based on model family, token per request, concurrency, and desired SLO. For example, for a rw-2-small quantized model with your profile, a 4-GPU pool with autoscaling to 8 during peaks is often enough. We include per-GPU throughput numbers in the sheet.
05:12 Olivia: rw-2-small? is that an internal name or a partner model?
05:16 Diego: It's our shorthand for a 7B-ish open model variant we commonly use in sims. Apologies on naming — transcription sometimes picks up our shorthand.
05:24 Sarah: Security: we need SOC2, SSO, and proof of no persistent customer PII logs on hosted — can you confirm?
05:31 Maya: Yes — Redwood provides SOC2 reports for enterprise, SAML SSO and RBAC controls in the console, and hosted retention settings with optional no-persist modes; we'll send the security pack. For Private on-prem you manage keys; for Dedicated we can integrate your KMS/HSM.
05:48 Tom: Network diagram — do you need firewall rules? We prefer port restrictions and a VPC peering approach if dedicated.
05:55 Maya: We'll include a sample network diagram for dedicated/VPC setup and the minimal firewall egress rules. Diego will add the port ranges.
06:02 Sarah: About the pilot — what does a 48-hour dedicated pilot look like?
06:06 Diego: We spin up a small dedicated pool mapped to your account, run a controlled benchmark of your traffic sample, collect KV hit rates, tails, and cost. We usually run two workloads: live traffic replay and synthetic burst tests. After 48 hours we produce a one-pager with expected savings and recommended config.
06:22 Maya: For success criteria let's capture: p50 < 200ms, cost per 1M tokens under $1,500 (example), and KV hit rate > 40%. If we hit those we can roll to a month-long pilot.
06:36 Olivia: That sounds fine. Make sure we can audit logs for any red flags — we need access logs for compliance.
06:41 Diego: Console exposes request-level traces, token-level cost breakdowns and you can export the logs to your SIEM.
06:49 Sarah: Any vendor lock-in if we go deep on Redwood runtime?
06:53 Maya: Redwood uses model-agnostic runtimes and supports multiple model families; we also give you model export configs. It's more about serving layer optimizations than model lock — but we will work with the team to document portability.
07:04 Tom: Competitors — Bedrock or Replicate — what are the big diffs here?
07:09 Maya: Bedrock handles model access but not the same production-focused batching/prefetch tooling and cost simulations. Replicate is great for model access but lacks the enterprise routing + caching playbook.
07:20 Sarah: Any gotchas we should watch for during the pilot?
07:24 Diego: Watch for session churn that lowers your prefix hit rate, and abrupt workload skews during promotions that can increase tail latency — we recommend scheduled cache warm-up and a canary ramp.
07:36 Maya: Ok I'll pause here and hand-off to Diego for the live Optimize demo showing the console suggestions.
07:42 Diego: (screen share) Here's the Optimize recommendations page, it lists batching window suggestions, expected savings, and a prefix cache config we can toggle. Note the confidence bar on each recommendation — we run sim and historical traffic to produce that.
08:05 Sarah: Is the confidence bar derived from real traces or just synthetic sim?
08:09 Diego: Mix of both. For customers we combine your real traces with Monte Carlo sims to estimate savings distribution. That's why we want your heatmap.
08:18 Tom: Can we change model variants mid-deploy if a quantized variant causes a regress?
08:22 Diego: Yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if regressions exceed thresholds. You define the evals and rollback triggers in the Console.
08:34 Sarah: Speaking of evals, can we tie quality alerts to our prompt test set?
08:38 Diego: Absolutely — Optimize can monitor a prompt set and trigger alerts on drift or percent drop in metric. We'll show a quick config after this.
08:46 (brief screen pause while Diego flips dashboard)
09:02 Diego: Here's a simulated run: enabling prefix cache at 50% hit and batching window 12ms — cost drops and p50 stays within target. Note the prefetch heatmap where we pre-warm hot session IDs before known peaks.
09:20 Tom: How is prefetch triggered? by user activity or scheduler?
09:24 Diego: Both. We have heuristics: on first N requests from a session we prefetch if the session has high probability of additional turns; you can also schedule prefetch for known surge windows.
09:35 Sarah: Any storage cost for KV? if we keep many session caches what's the cost?
09:39 Diego: KV resides in GPU RAM for the worker. Storage cost is mostly memory footprint; we account for this in the dedicated sizing and charge accordingly. We'll show per-GPU memory utilization in the benchmark results.
09:51 Olivia: For the pilot, can we run our full data (with PII) or should it be anonymized?
09:56 Maya: For hosted we advise anonymized or synthetic; for dedicated we can do redacted PII or on-prem. We'll include guidance in the security pack.
10:05 Sarah: Anything else on the console?
10:08 Diego: Quick demo of the cost spreadsheet generator — you can upload traffic profile and Optimize spits out per-model and per-route cost breakdown. (shows table) You can toggle hit rate assumptions to see sensitivity.
10:22 Maya: Ok we're running into time; quick recap and next steps.
10:26 Sarah: Yes please.
10:27 Maya: Recap: 1) We'll send tailored cost spreadsheet and runbook; 2) Diego to set up 48-hr dedicated pilot and benchmark; 3) Security pack including SOC2, SAML/SSO, network diagram, and KMS notes; 4) Customer to confirm traffic sample and heatmap.
10:43 Olivia: Agreed. Also want the canary rollback playbook.
10:46 Diego: We'll include that in the runbook.
10:48 Maya: Great. I'll send calendar invite for pilot kickoff and include Tom and Diego. Any final Qs?
10:55 Sarah: None from me, thanks.
10:58 Olivia: Thanks everyone.
11:00 End recording

Action items noted in call: Maya to send cost spreadsheet by 2026-07-23; Diego to schedule pilot week of Aug 3; Sarah to share heatmap by 2026-07-28.

Links referenced: Optimize playbook slide deck (internal link), cost-model-generator spreadsheet (will be shared), security pack (to be sent).

Notes about transcript quality: occasional shorthand (rw-2-small), some speaker overlap at ~07:20, numbers are illustrative until Diego runs exact sims.
